scope: The StegVerse ecosystem maintains its own KV (SVKV) as a KV user like any other: its own WorkSpace/Org, its own ##_<name> storage locations and its own SKAP Vault inside KV, reached through KV's InTr from at minimum a healthy node. KV stays independent of the ecosystem Orgs: it keeps its own ledger behind its own InTr ingress/egress endpoint (endpoint_kind KV), never on any Org ledger ref, and Org/KV interactions are linked receipts in each side's own ledger with nothing copied across. KV is a governed layer over storage the user already owns, reached through a GATEWAY node: SVKV's storage is the StegVerse@gmail.com Google Drive, which holds only encrypted contents, and the external storage's own records never cross into KV. KV's ledger lives as encrypted, content-addressed objects in that storage, verified on KV's side; every KV ledger head is signed, each InTr exchange with an Org records the KV head digest in the Org-side linked receipt, KV refuses any head older than the newest one an Org has recorded (KV_LEDGER_HEAD_ROLLBACK_DETECTED), and an empty or missing ledger is never taken as a genesis. The SKAP root key stays in TV/TVC custody; SKAP holds only wrapped data keys and the vault never holds the credential needed to reach it. Done: the ecosystem's WorkSpace is registered in KV, and one ecosystem credential goes from a receipted SKAP Vault custody record to a layer-2 ALLOW, end to end, on real KV ledger inputs. Anything beyond that is a new registered task (multi-provider redundancy included).
